close_reason: Implemented Option A per user direction. Added pkix-revocation::OutOfScopeReason enum (CrlOnlyAttributeCerts/CrlOnlyUserCerts/CrlOnlyCaCerts) and pkix-revocation::Error::OutOfScope(OutOfScopeReason) variant. CrlChecker::check_revocation and check_revocation_against_anchor now return Err(OutOfScope(reason)) at all 6 IDP scope-mismatch sites instead of the historic ambiguous Ok(()). Trait doc rewritten: Ok(()) is now unambiguous 'verified not-revoked'; not-covered surfaces as Err(OutOfScope) for CRL or Err(OcspStatusUnknown) for OCSP. Hard-fail callers can now treat any non-Ok as failure; soft-fail callers can match on the OutOfScopeReason. PKITS §4.14.11/12/14 tests updated to assert specific Err(OutOfScope(reason)) outcomes; §4.14.13 confirmed correctly returns Ok() (cert IS a CA per OpenSSL oracle, despite EE suffix). External oracle (openssl x509 -text) used to verify cert types — corrected the original test author's misclassification of fixtures 11 and 13 as end-entities. No tests deleted, skipped, or weakened; assertions strengthened (specific reason vs. opaque Ok()).
description:
pkix-revocation/src/lib.rs:282-296 documents that `check_revocation` returning `Ok(())` has dual semantics — 'not revoked' OR 'not covered (out of scope)' — and tells callers:

  > Callers enforcing a hard-fail revocation policy must separately verify that
  > at least one revocation source actually covers the certificate in question.

This advice is unactionable from the public API. There is no method on `RevocationChecker`, `CrlChecker`, or `OcspChecker` that exposes scope coverage. A caller that wants 'hard-fail unless revocation actually covered this cert' has no programmatic way to check.

The CRL implementation (pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:274-294) returns Ok(()) on three IDP scope mismatches (only_contains_attribute_certs, only_contains_user_certs, only_contains_ca_certs). These are exactly the cases where a caller might want to know 'this CRL did not actually decide anything for this cert'.

Fix options:

A. (preferred) Add a new error variant `Error::OutOfScope { reason: ... }` and convert the three `return Ok(())` sites in crl.rs to it. Hard-fail callers get an unambiguous Err; soft-fail callers can match on it and treat as Ok. This is a breaking change to RevocationChecker semantics — schedule for next minor.

B. Add a separate predicate method to RevocationChecker (e.g. `covers(&self, cert, issuer) -> bool`) so callers can pre-flight scope before calling `check_revocation`.

C. Document this as a known limitation with a worked example for hard-fail callers (parse the IDP themselves).

Severity: P3 / opinion. Functionally the doc is honest about the limitation; the issue is that the documented mitigation can't actually be performed by an external caller without parsing the CRL themselves.

Pass-1 attribution: pass-1 P2 fix (PKIX-d667) made the parse-error path fail-closed, but did not address the more fundamental Ok(()) ambiguity for scope mismatches.
notes: DEFERRED by /do-beads pass: this is a design-choice issue requiring human direction. Option A (Error::OutOfScope variant) is a behavior-changing API revision with downstream impact (every CrlChecker caller's match arms shift). Option B (covers() predicate) adds a trait method requiring non-trivial logic for CRL+OCSP. Option C (docs only) is partially in place. Per project AGENTS.md, this kind of API-shape decision is out of scope for /do-beads — needs explicit human direction. Leaving open.
title: P3: pkix-revocation RevocationChecker::check_revocation Ok(()) dual-semantics is unactionable from caller side
